The best performing turbine at Penmanshiel farm is Penmanshiel_13 with a capacity factor of 0.3161. The worst performing turbine is Penmanshiel_07 with a capacity factor of 0.2163.
The global wake effect at Kelmarsh farm, as a percentage of the annual energy yield, is 7.778%. This is based on the long-term (LT) wake losses provided in the operational assessment.

The gearbox of the turbine is a custom-built, three-stage planetary-helical design. This design allows for a compact, high-performance construction with high torque, which is ideal for the turbine's operational needs. The turbine shuts down at a wind speed of approximately 25 m/s to prevent damage. This is in line with standard practices to protect the turbine from extreme weather conditions.

The long-term annual energy production (AEP) estimates for Penmanshiel are as follows:

- P50: 76.623 GWh
- P90: 75.67 GWh

These estimates are based on a daily generalized additive model (GAM) temperature approach, which considers multiple factors affecting the farm's energy production.

The EnergyUp Full Power Curve Advanced upgrade is compatible with the MM82, MM92, and MM100 turbines. This upgrade increases the Annual Energy Production (AEP) by optimizing torque and rotor speed. Specifically, for the MM92 turbine, the power output can be increased to 2.2 MW (for the 50 Hz market) and 2.125 MW (for the 60 Hz market). The AEP boost from this upgrade can be up to 5% depending on the turbine model and wind farm conditions.

The ScotWind leasing round requires applicants to submit several key documents and information. I will present this information as per the technical documents found. </thinking>
Here is what an applicant has to submit in the ScotWind leasing round, according to the ScotWind Leasing - April 2019 update (working draft), p.2:

- Project concept
- Project delivery plan
- Capability and experience
- Development budget
- Developer financial resources
- Commitment to the project and preparedness

Additionally, applicants may be asked to complete an application form and provide separate substantive documents, including those outlined in Table 1 of the ScotWind Leasing - April 2019 update (working draft), p.2. If an application involves more than one legal entity, statements of commitment at board level are required (ScotWind Leasing - April 2019 update (working draft), p.2).

You can find more details in the ScotWind Leasing - April 2019 update (working draft): https://www.crownestatescotland.com/sites/default/files/2023-07/scotwind-leasing-april-2019-update.pdf
